RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Defense Pilot Program to Acquire Innovative Commercial Items (DFARS Case 2017-D029)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing an interim rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 879 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017. Section 879 authorizes the Secretary of Defense and the Secretaries of the military departments to carry out a pilot program to be known as the "defense commercial solutions opening pilot program.” Under the pilot program, DoD may acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services using a competitive procedure called a commercial solutions opening (CSO). Under a CSO, DoD may competitively select proposals received in response to a general solicitation based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers. This pilot program is designed to test whether streamlined procedures, similar to broad agency announcements for acquisitions of basic and applied research, are effective for acquiring innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. DoD intends to publish an interim rule in order to allow DoD to immediately implement and utilize the pilot program. This will allow DoD to assess the feasibility and advisability of acquiring innovative commercial items, technologies, or services in accordance with the streamlined procedures of the pilot program prior to expiration of the program authority on September 30, 2022.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Products and Services From Africa (DFARS Case 2017-D030)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 899A of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2017.  Section 899A provides enhanced authority to acquire the products or services of covered African countries in support of DoD activities in Africa and repeals section 1263 of the NDAA for FY 2015.  This rule will allow contracting officers to limit competition to, or provide a preference for, the products or services of covered African countries.  This authority may only be used in support of covered activities in covered African countries after approval of a written determination.  In addition, this authority cannot be used for the procurement of any goods on the procurement list maintained by the Committee for Purchase From People Who Are Blind or Severely Disabled.

The rule has a limited application to products and services of Africa in support of covered activities in covered African countries. The priority sourcing of products or services produced in countries where the United States has long-term agreements is an important element of maintaining trust relationships that support United States participation in counterterrorism efforts and humanitarian response by United States Government agencies.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Service Contract Reporting (DFARS Case 2017-D035)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 812 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017.  Section 812 requires the Secretary of Defense to:

  • Establish a data collection system with regard to each purchase of services by a military department or defense agency in excess of $3 million for the following service acquisition portfolio groups:  logistics management services, equipment-related services, knowledge-based services, and electronics and communications services; and
  • Prepare an annual inventory, and submit to Congress a summary of the inventory, of activities performed during the preceding fiscal year pursuant to staff augmentation contracts on behalf of DoD.

To create the inventory required by the statute, DoD must collect information from contractors performing such services, which will be accomplished through the use of the Enterprise-wide Contractor Manpower Reporting Application (ECMRA).  This rule amends the DFARS to provide instructions to contracting officers and contractors regarding reports to be submitted through ECMRA.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Past Performance Information Retrieval System--Statistical Reporting (DFARS Case 2017-D003)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to incorporate price risk, item risk, and supplier risk factors into DFARS 252.213-7000, Notice to Prospective Suppliers on Use of Past Performance Information Retrieval System-Statistical Reporting in Past Performance Evaluations. The Past Performance Information Retrieval System-Statistical Reporting (PPIRS-SR) application provides objective, statistical information that can be used by contracting officers for evaluation of contractor quotations under simplified acquisition procedures.  This rule is necessary in order to align the DFARS with enhancements made to the PPIRS-SR application in 2016, enhancements that better enable DoD to evaluate supplier past performance in order to prevent the acquisition of counterfeit parts. PPIRS-SR captures historical pricing data from various sources to compute "average price" paid, applies a common statistical methodology to derive an expected cost range for previously procured items, and alerts contracting officers to items considered "high-risk" (i.e., the item to be procured has a critical use or is susceptible to counterfeiting).
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Submission of Summary Subcontract Report (DFARS Case 2017-D005)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to clarify the entity to which Summary Subcontract Reports (SSRs) are to be submitted and the entity that acknowledges receipt of, or rejects, SSRs in the Electronic Subcontracting Reporting System (eSRS). The SSR is used to collect prime contractors’ and subcontractors’ subcontract award data for a specific Federal Government agency when the prime or subcontractor: (a) holds one or more contracts over $700,000 (over $1,500,000 for construction of a public facility); and (b) is required to report subcontracts awarded to various types of small business under an individual subcontracting plan with the Federal Government. Currently, the contractors submit the SSR to the various individual DoD components (i.e., departments and agencies within DoD) with which they have contracts. As a result of this rule, contractors with individual subcontracting plans will submit a single, consolidated SSR in eSRS at the DoD-level, which will be acknowledged or rejected in eSRS at the DoD-level. These revisions will bring DFARS into compliance with the requirement for a consolidated SSR in the clause at Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan. This rule will also have a positive impact on contractors, because they will be able to submit a single consolidated SSR to DoD, instead of multiple SSRs to DoD components.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Electronic Submission and Processing of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports (DFARS Case 2016-D032)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to update and clarify exceptions to the use of Wide Area WorkFlow (WAWF) for electronic submission and processing of payment requests and receiving reports. The rule will amend the DFARS to reflect the current exceptions to WAWF, which include classified contracts; when contractor submission of electronic payment requests and receiving reports is not feasible; when the contracting officer grants permission for the contractor to submit payment requests and receiving reports by specific, temporary, non-electronic means; or when DoD is unable to receive a payment request or provide acceptance in electronic form. The proposed rule also updates DFARS Appendix F and removes obsolete language from DFARS 246.370 and its related clause at DFARS 252.246-7000, Material Inspection and Receiving Report.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Antiterrorism Training Requirements for Contractors (DFARS Case 2017-D034)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement requirements of DoD Instruction O-2000.16, "DoD Antiterrorism (AT) Program Implementation: DoD AT Standards," as it relates to contractors.  Specifically, DoDI O-2000.16 requires that contractor and subcontractor employees who, as a condition of contract performance, require routine physical access to a federally controlled facility or military installation for a period of performance in excess of 6 months, complete Level I antiterrorism awareness training annually. This rule creates a new DFARS contract clause to inform contractors of this mandatory training requirement.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Payment Instructions (DFARS Case 2017-D036)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement recommendations of representatives from Defense Finance Accounting Services, the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense Comptroller, and DoD Chief Financial Officer, the military services, and Defense Procurement and Acquisition Policy, which concluded that the appropriate accounting treatment for payments can be derived from the type of item acquired and the type of payment.  The rule proposes instructions for payment offices to allocate payments to the correct accounting classifications when making payments on contracts with multiple accounting classifications.  The rule also proposes instructions for contractors when submitting progress payment requests for contracts that identify multiple production lots.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Contractor Purchasing System Review Threshold (DFARS Case 2017-D038)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to establish a higher dollar threshold for conducting contractor purchasing system reviews. This rule proposes, in lieu of the threshold at Federal Acquisition Regulation 44.302(a) of $25 million, the administrative contracting officer shall determine the need for a contractors purchasing system review if a contractor’s sales to the Government are expected to exceed $50 million during the next 12 months.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Source of Photovoltaic Devices (DFARS Case 2018-D007)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a proposed rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 813(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018.  Section 813(b) repeals section 858 of the NDAA for FY 2015, but does not repeal section 846 of the NDAA for FY 2011. By reverting to section 846 of the NDAA for FY 2011, the restriction on acquisition of photovoltaic devices by contractors is now applicable only if the photovoltaic device is installed on DoD property or in a facility owned by DoD  and reserved for the exclusive use of DoD for the full economic life of the device, whereas under section 858 of the NDAA for FY 2015, the restriction was applicable if either condition applied.

Section 846 requires compliance with the Buy American Act; whereas section 858 imposed a requirement for manufacture in the U.S. separate from the Buy American Act, and was therefore no longer covered by the existing exceptions to and waivers of the Buy American Act (such as a waiver on the basis of "unreasonable cost" or "inconsistent with the public interest" (for acquiring photovoltaic devices from qualifying countries or U.S.-made photovoltaic devices when the WTO GPA applies). With the repeal of section 858, it will no longer be necessary to do individual case-by-case waivers for waivers based on unreasonable cost or inconsistent with the public interest. Also with the repeal of section 858, the waiver of the component test for photovoltaic devices is reinstated, since they are commercially available off-the-shelf items, for which the component test is waived under the Buy American Act.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Undefinitized Contract Actions (DFARS Case 2018-D008)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a proposed rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 815 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018 and section 811 of the NDAA for FY 2017, which amends 10 U.S.C. 2326 to revise requirements for undefinitized contract actions (UCA).  This proposed rule requires the following:

  • If a contractor submits a qualifying proposal to definitize a UCA and the contracting officer definitizes the contract after the end of the 180-day period beginning on the date on which the contractor submitted the qualifying proposal, the head of the agency concerned shall ensure that the profit allowed on the contract accurately reflects the cost risk of the contractor as such risk existed on the date the contractor submitted the qualifying proposal.
  • No UCA may extend beyond 90 days without a written determination by the secretary of the military department, head of the defense agency, combatant commander, or Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics). 
  • Contracting officers may not enter into a UCA for a foreign military sales unless the contractual action provides for agreement upon contractual terms, specifications, and price by the end of the 180-day period.

This rule does not revise the current regulatory requirements at DFARS 215.404-71-3(d)(2), which directs contracting officers to assess the extent to which costs have been incurred prior to definitization of the UCA.  However, contracting officers must document their assessment in formulating negotiation profit objectives that the profit allowed on the contract accurately reflects the cost risk of the contractor as such risk existed on the date the contractor submitted the qualifying proposal.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Post-Award Debriefings (DFARS Case 2018-D009)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 818 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018.  Section 818 requires amendment of the DFARS to provide enhanced post-award debriefing rights for certain DoD contracts and task or delivery orders that exceed $10 million.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Restrictions on Use of Lowest Price Technically Acceptable Source Selection Process (DFARS Case 2018-D010)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement sections 822, 832, and 882 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018 and sections 813, 814, and 892 of the NDAA for FY 2017.  These sections establish minimum requirements for the use of the lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA) sources selection procedures, as well as specific restrictions on the use of LPTA procedures in acquisitions:

  • Where DoD would realize no, or minimal, additional innovation or future technological advantage by using a different methodology;
  • Where the goods procured are predominantly expendable in nature, are non technical, or have a short life expectancy or short shelf life;
  • For major defense acquisition programs;
  • For aviation critical safety items;
  • Predominantly for information technology services, cybersecurity services, systems engineering and technical assistance services, advanced electronic testing, audit or audit readiness services, or other knowledge-based professional services;
  • Predominantly for personal protective equipment;
  • Predominantly for knowledge-based training or logistics services in contingency operations or other operations outside the United States, including in Afghanistan or Iraq;
  • For auditing services and audit readiness services; and
  • For personal protective equipment, when the level of quality or failure of the item could result in combat casualties.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Exemption From Design-Build Selection Procedures (DFARS Case 2018-D011)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 823 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018.  Section 823 amends 10 U.S.C. 2305a to provide exemptions from design-build selection procedures for contracts that exceed $4 million.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Contract Closeout Authority (DFARS Case 2018-D012)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 836 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2017, as amended by section 824 of the NDAA for FY 2018. Section 836 permits contracting officers to close out contracts or groups of contracts through issuance of a modification of each contract action without completing a reconciliation audit or other corrective action, provided the contract:

  • Was entered into prior to fiscal year 2000;
  • Has no further supplies or services deliverables due under the terms and conditions; and
  • Is not otherwise reconcilable, because either contract records have been destroyed or lost or the time, or the effort required to establish the exact amount owed the U.S. Government or to the contractor is disproportionate to the amount at issue.

This rule will expedite closeout of the covered contract actions.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 837 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018.  Section 837 requires amendment of the DFARS to provide for the appropriate use of the should-cost review process of a major weapon system.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Acquisition of Commercial Items (DFARS Case 2018-D016)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement the requirements of sections 847 and 848 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018 and sections 871 and 872, 876 and 877, and 878 of the NDAA for FY 2017 to provide regulatory requirements that state:

  • How contracting officers may require the offeror to submit relevant information to support market research for price analysis;
  • That an offeror may submit information or analysis relating to the value of a commercial item to aid in the determination of the reasonableness of the price of such item, and a contracting officer may consider such information or analysis pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 2379;
  • That the head of an agency may not enter into a contract for facilities-related services, knowledge-based services (except engineering services), construction services, medical services, or transportation services that are not commercial services unless it is determined in writing by the appropriate authority that no commercial services are suitable to meet the agency's needs;
  • That items valued at less than $10,000 that are purchased by a contractor for use in the performance of multiple contracts with DoD and other parties and are not identifiable to any particular contract shall be treated as a commercial item; and
  • That services provided by a business unit that is a nontraditional defense contractor (as that term is defined in 10 U.S.C. 2302(9)) shall be treated as commercial items, to the extent that such services use the same pool of employees as used for commercial customers and are priced using methodology similar to methodology used for commercial pricing.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Definition of "Competitive Procedures" (DFARS Case 2018-D021)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 221 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018.  Section 221 expands the definition of 'competitive procedures" to include the competitive selection for award of science and technology proposals. Specifically, section 221 replaces the words "basic research" with "science and technology" in the definition of "competitive procedures" at 10 U.S.C. 2302(2)(B).

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Applicability of Inflation Adjustments of Acquisition-Related Thresholds (DFARS Case 2018-D023)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 821 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 regarding DoD-unique thresholds.  Section 821 amends 41 U.S.C. 1908(d) to make inflation adjustments of statutory acquisition-related thresholds under 41 U.S.C. 1908(d) applicable to existing contracts and subcontracts in effect on the date of the adjustment.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Modification of DFARS Clause "Surge Option" (DFARS Case 2018-D025)

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Modification of DFARS clause "Transportation of Supplies By Sea" (DFARS Case 2018-D028)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to modify the contract clause 252.247-7023, Transportation of Supplies by Sea. RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Promoting Voluntary Post-Award Disclosure of Defective Pricing (DFARS Case 2015-D030)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to promote voluntary contractor disclosures of defective pricing identified by the contractor after contract award by providing DoD contracting officers with the discretion to request a limited-scope audit or a full-scope audit as appropriate for the circumstances, thereby reducing repeated contractor submissions of certified cost or pricing data.  The DFARS rule supplements Federal Acquisition Regulation 15.407-1(c) to indicate that, in the interest of promoting voluntary disclosures of defective pricing identified by the contractor, DoD contracting officers shall request a limited-scope audit, unless a full-scope audit is appropriate for the circumstances. 

One respondent submitted a public comment in response to the proposed rule. This rule will apply to all DoD contractors, including small entities, who are required to submit certified cost or pricing data.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Food Services for Dining Facilities on Military Installations (DFARS Case 2015-D012)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to provide policy and procedures for soliciting offers, evaluating proposals, and awarding contracts for the operation of a military dining facility pursuant to the Randolph-Sheppard Act(20 U.S.C. 107, et seq.). This final rule amends the DFARS to implement the Joint Report and Policy Statement (Joint Policy Statement) issued by DoD, the Department of Education, and the CFP pursuant to section 848 of the NDAA for FY 2006. Pursuant to the Joint Policy Statement, the Randolph-Sheppard Act applies to contracts for the operation of a military dining facility, also known as full food services, while the Committee for Purchase from People Who Are Blind or Severely Disabled statute applies to contracts and subcontracts for dining support services (including mess attendant services).
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Independent Research and Development Expenses (DFARS Case 2016-D017)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to ensure that substantial future independent research and development (IR&D) expenses, as a means to reduce evaluated bid prices in competitive source selections, are evaluated in a uniform way during competitive source selections.  This rule is intended to address situations when promised future IR&D expenditures (funded through allowable IR&D overhead expenses) are used to substantially reduce bid prices and gain a competitive advantages on competitive procurements.  As a result of this rule, DoD contracting officers will adjust the total evaluated price of major defense acquisition programs and major automated information systems proposals, for evaluation purposes only, to include the amount by which the offerors propose that future IR&D investments reduce the price of the proposals. 

Sixteen respondents submitted public comments in response to the proposed rule.  This rule is not expected to impose costs on offerors.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Amendments Related to Sources of Electronic Parts (DFARS Case 2016-D013)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 885(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2016, which amends section 818(c)(3)(D)(iii) of the NDAA for FY 2012 to make contractor and subcontractor identification and use of contractor-approved distributors subject to approval (as well as review and audit) by appropriate DoD officials. Contractors are only allowed to use contractor-approved suppliers when electronic parts are not in production by the original manufacturer or an authorized aftermarket manufacturer, and are not currently available in stock from the original manufacturer, its authorized suppliers, or suppliers that obtain such parts exclusively from the original manufacturers of the parts or their authorized suppliers.  The contractor may proceed with the acquisition of electronic parts from a contractor-approved supplier unless otherwise notified by DoD. Five respondents submitted comments on the proposed rule.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Undefinitized Contract Action Definitization (DFARS Case 2015-D024)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to revise the DD Form 1547, Record of Weighted Guidelines, to provide a more transparent means of documenting costs incurred during the undefinitized period of an undefinitized contract action (UCA), and to recognize when contractors demonstrate efficient management and internal cost control systems through the submittal of a timely, auditable proposal in furtherance of definitization of a UCA. This rule revises processes that are internal to the Government to provide a more transparent means of documenting the impact of costs incurred during the undefinitized period of a UCA when calculating negotiation profit objectives.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Use of the Government Property Clause (DFARS Case 2015-D035)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to expand the prescription for use of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.245-1, Government Property, to apply to all purchase orders for repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification to Government property, regardless of the acquisition cost of the items to be repaired.   Currently, the FAR clause is optional for use in purchase orders for repair when the acquisition cost of the item to be repaired is less than the simplified acquisition threshold; however, acquisition cost alone is not an indicator of the criticality or sensitivity of the property.  The acquisition cost of individual items of firearms, body armor, night-vision equipment, computers, or cryptologic devices may be below the simplified acquisition threshold, but the accountability requirements for these items are fairly stringent.  Requiring the clause in all purchase orders for repair, regardless of the acquisition cost of the item to be repaired, will ensure DoD has better accountability and insight into military reparable assets. 

This rule will increase costs for contractors, including small entities, who receive purchase orders for repair of Government property, because these contractors will be required to comply with the reporting requirements associated with the Government property clause.  However, the rule also provides the contractors with the protections of the Government property clause (where the Government self-insures the property provided to the contractor), and provides DoD with better accountability for its property.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Micro-Purchase Threshold (DFARS Case 2017-D027)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement sections 217(a) and 821 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017.  Section 821 increases the micro-purchase threshold for DoD procurements to $5,000.  Section 217(a) further increases the micro-purchase threshold to $10,000 for purposes of DoD basic research programs and for the activities of the DoD science and technology reinvention laboratories.  To implement sections 217(a) and 821, this rule will amend DFARS subpart 202.1 to add a DoD-unique definition of micro-purchase threshold, to be used in lieu of the Federal Acquisition Regulation definition for DoD procurements.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Delegation of Special Emergency Procurement Authority (DFARS Case 2018-D024)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to delegate to the head of the contracting activity the decision authorities provided to the head of the agency by sections 816 and 1641 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018.2018 Specifically, sections 816 and 1641 add new special emergency procurement authorities for certain acquisitions, to include that that are determined by the head of the agency to facilitate defense against or recovery from cyber attack; facilitate the provision of international disaster assistance; or support response to an emergency or major disaster. These special emergency authorities are being implemented in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) under FAR Case 2018-009. This rule will supplement the FAR rule by delegating the authority from the head of the agency to the head of the contracting activity. This rule also makes conforming changes to nonstatutory emergency acquisition flexibilities relating to item-unique identification, receipt of only one offer, and limitations on time-andmaterials contracts.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Repeal of DFARS Clause "Pricing Adjustments" (DFARS Case 2018-D032)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to repeal the clause at DFARS 252.217-7000, Pricing Adjustments. The repeal of this DFARS clause supports a recommendation from the DoD Regulatory Reform Task Force. On February 24, 2017, the President signed Executive Order 13777, Enforcing the Regulatory Reform Agenda, "which established a Federal policy to alleviate unnecessary regulatory burdens” on the American people. In accordance with Executive Order 13777, DoD established a Regulatory Reform Task Force to review and validate DoD regulations, including the DFARS, to determine if revisions were needed. A public notice of the establishment of the DFARS Subgroup to the DoD Regulatory Reform Task Force, for the purpose of reviewing DFARS provisions and clauses, was published in the Federal Register at 82 FR 35741 on August 1, 2017, and requested public input on all DFARS clauses and provisions. No public comments were received on this particular clause.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Repeal of DFARS clause "Indefinite Quantities-No Fixed Charges" (DFARS Case 2018-D034)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to repeal the contract clause 252.247-7005, Indefinite Quantities No Fixed Charges. Descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and negotiated costs are contained in the contract’s incorporated schedule of rates. Stevedoring services are ordered utilizing this information. When services are delivered and invoiced by the contractor, in accordance with the contract, and certified by the contract officer representative, the invoice is paid. The clause provides no additional benefit for the contractor or the Government. The DFARS clause is unnecessary and can be removed. The removal of this DFARS text supports a recommendation from the DoD Regulatory Reform Task Force. RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to repeal the contract clause 252.247-7024, Notification of Transportation of Supplies by Sea. RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Temporary Extension of Test Program for Comprehensive Small Business Subcontracting Plans (DFARS Case 2015-D013)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 821 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for fiscal year (FY) 2015, section 872 of the NDAA for FY 2016, and section 826 of the NDAA for FY 2017. Implementation of these sections in the DFARS is necessary to:

  • Require contractors with comprehensive subcontracting plans to report additional information on a semiannual basis in order to evaluate the effectiveness of the program;
  • Reinstate liquidated damages under comprehensive subcontracting plans
  • Require consideration, as part of the past performance evaluation of an offeror, of any failure to make a good faith effort to comply with its comprehensive subcontracting plan
  • Increase the threshold for participation in the Test Program from $5 million to $100 million;
    Prohibit negotiation of comprehensive subcontracting plans with contractors who failed to meet the subcontracting goals of their comprehensive subcontracting plan for the prior fiscal year;
  • Remove the prohibition on negotiation of comprehensive subcontracting plans with contractors who failed to meet the subcontracting goals of their comprehensive subcontracting plan for the prior fiscal year; and
  • Extend the Test Program through December 31, 2027.

This rule will streamline regulatory requirements, reduce costs for the nine large businesses participating in the Test Program, and encourage Test Program participants to make a good faith effort to comply with their comprehensive small business subcontracting plans.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Procurement of Commercial Items (DFARS Case 2016-D006)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD issued a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement the requirements of sections 851 through 853 and 855 through 857 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2016, as well as the requirements of section 831 of the NDAA for FY 2013 related to the procurement of commercial items.  DoD previously published a proposed rule on August 3, 2015, under DFARS case 2013-D034 (80 FR 45918), to implement the requirements of section 831. Based on the comments received in response to that proposed rule, and in order to implement the requirements of the NDAA for FY 2016, DFARS case 2013-D034 was closed into this rule. This DFARS rule accomplishes the following:

  • Provides guidance to contracting officers for making price reasonableness determinations;
  • Promotes consistency in making commercial item determinations; and
  • Expands opportunities for nontraditional defense contractors to do business with DoD by permitting the use of commercial item procurement procedures when acquiring goods and services from nontraditional defense contractors. 

Eleven respondents submitted public comments on the proposed rule.  DoD expects that this rule will decrease costs for contractors by promoting consistency among contracting officers with regard to commercial item determinations and allowing the use of commercial item procedures when procuring from nontraditional defense contractors, which will reduce the number of procurements that require the submission of certified cost or pricing data.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Amendment to Mentor-Protégé Program (DFARS Case 2016-D011)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement section 861 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year (FY) 2016, which provides the following amendments to the DoD Pilot Mentor-Protégé Program (the Program):

  • Requires mentor firms to report assistance provided to or obtained for protégé firms; new subcontracts awarded to protégé firms; any extensions, increases in the scope of work, or additional, unreported payments to protégé firms; all Federal contracts awarded to the mentor and protégé firms as a joint venture; whether the terms of the mentor-protégé agreement have changed; and a narrative describing the success assistance provided under the Program has had in addressing the protégé firm's developmental needs, the impact on DoD contracts, and addressing any problems encountered.
  • Requires mentor firms and protégé firms to meet new eligibility criteria.
  • Limits the number of mentor-protégé agreements to which a protégé firm may be a party to one at a time.
  • Limits the period of time during which a protégé firm may participate in mentor-protégé agreements under the Program to 5 years.
  • Requires mentor-protégé agreements to address the benefits of the agreement to DoD and goals for additional awards for which the protégé firm can compete outside the Program.
  • Removes business development assistance using mentor firm personnel and cash in exchange for an ownership interest in the protégé firm from the types of assistance that a mentor firm may provide to a protégé firm.
  • Prohibits reimbursement of any fee assessed by the mentor firm for certain services provided to the protégé firm while participating in a joint venture with the protégé firm.

This rule will slightly increase the costs for contractors participating in the program by introducing new reporting requirements, as required by the statute; however, these costs are offset by benefits offered by the Program.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Competition for Religious-Related Services Contracts (DFARS Case 2016-D015)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement section 898 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016, which prohibits DoD from precluding a nonprofit organization from competing for a contract for religious-related services on a U.S. military installation.  The rule implements the prohibition set forth in the statute.  In addition, since solicitations that are set aside for small businesses are likely to provide a competitive environment that excludes participation of nonprofit organizations, the rule provides a new provision to be used in solicitations for religious-related services on a U.S. military installation that are set aside for small businesses in order to advise potential offerors that nonprofit organizations will not be precluded from competing.  Contracting officers are also directed to not use any of the sole source authorities at Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-5(b)(4) through (7), since use of those authorities would restrict award of the requirement to a small business and, contrary to statute, would bar a nonprofit organization from being considered for the award.  

There were no public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.  This rule will not increase the cost of contracting for contractors. However, this rule may have an economic impact on small entities, since the rule expands opportunities for nonprofit organizations that will now be authorized to compete on solicitations that are set aside for small businesses, when the acquisition of religious-related services on a U.S. military installation.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Definition of "Information Technology" (DFARS Case 2017-D033)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to make a technical correction to relocate the definition of "information technology" from DFARS 202.101 to DFARS 239.7301.  The definition of information technology was established in section 806 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011.  Section 806(b)(6) used the definition of information technology in 40 U.S.C. 11101(6) to define a covered item of supply.  On October 30, 2015, DoD published in the Federal Register (80 FR 67244) the final rule for DFARS Case 2012-D050, Requirements Relating to Supply Chain Risk, incorporating the definition of information technology into DFARS 202.101, as opposed to DFARS 239.7301.  This proposed change will align the definition of information technology with DFARS 239.73, Requirements for Information Relating to Supply Chain Risk, as originally intended in section 806.  There is no cost impact on contractors or offerors.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Consolidation of Contract Requirements (DFARS Case 2017-D004)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to remove outdated DFARS coverage regarding consolidation of contract requirements. DFARS 207.170, Consolidation of contract requirements, defines consolidation as "the use of a solicitation to obtain offers for a single contract or multiple award contract to satisfy two or more requirements of a department, agency, or activity for supplies or services that previously have been provided to, or performed for, that department, agency, or activity under two or more separate contracts." DFARS 207.170 also contains procedures for contracting officers to follow when a requirement for supplies or services meets the definition of consolidation. Section 1671 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 repealed consolidated contract requirements under 10 U.S.C. 2382. In addition, section 1671 amended section 44 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 657q) to remove the requirement for DoD to comply with 10 U.S.C. 2382. As a result, DoD is now required to comply with 15 U.S.C. 657q, which places limitations on the use of acquisition strategies involving the consolidation of contract requirements. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) addresses consolidation, including the limitations imposed by 15 U.S.C. 657q, at FAR 7.107. By removing the outdated DFARS coverage of consolidation, this rule will reduce confusion among the DoD contracting workforce caused by similar requirements in the FAR and DFARS.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: New Qualifying Country--Latvia (DFARS Case 2017-D037)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD issued a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to add Latvia as a qualifying country. On April 10, 2017, the U.S. Secretary of Defense signed a new reciprocal defense procurement agreement with Latvia. The agreement removes discriminatory barriers to procurements of supplies and services produced by industrial enterprises of the other country to the extent mutually beneficial and consistent with national laws, regulations, policies, and international obligations. The agreement does not cover construction or construction material. Latvia is already a designated country under the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Educational Service Agreements (DFARS Case 2017-D039)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is issuing a final rule to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to delete language at DFARS 237.7202(a), which prohibits the use of Educational Services Agreements (ESAs) as a contracting method for training in the legal profession, except when in connection with the detailing of commissioned officers to law schools under 10 U.S.C. 2004. An ESA is an ordering agreement under which the Government may acquire educational services. DFARS 237.72 prescribes policies and procedures for acquiring educational services from schools, colleges, universities, or other educational institutions, including the use of ESAs. Paragraph (a) of DFARS 237.7202 prohibits the use of ESAs as a contracting method for training in the legal profession, except when in connection with the detailing of commissioned officers to law schools under 10 U.S.C. 2004. This limitation was established at a time when legal training was acquired only for the purpose of obtaining doctorate degrees for military judge advocates. DoD’s need for legal training has evolved since the implementation of the text at DFARS 237.7202(a). As 10 U.S.C. 2004 contains no prohibition against acquiring other training in the legal profession, the rule will delete the language at DFARS 237.7202(a) to allow DoD to make agreements that permit payment for master of laws degrees and other legal training needs, in accordance with applicable law, regulation, and policy.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: State Sponsor of Terrorism--North Korea (DFARS Case 2018-D004)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD issued a final rule amending the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement the designation by the Department of State of North Korea as a state sponsor of terrorism. This final rule adds North Korea to the list of countries that are state sponsors of terrorism in the definition of "state sponsor of terrorism" in paragraph (a) of the provisions at DFARS 252.225-7049, Prohibition on Acquisition of Commercial Satellite Services from Certain Foreign Entities-Representation, and DFARS 252.225-7050, Disclosure of Ownership or Control by the Government of a Country that is a State Sponsor of Terrorism. The provision at DFARS 252.225-7050 implements 10 U.S.C. 2327, which prohibits DoD from entering into a contract with a firm that is owned or controlled by the government of a country that is a state sponsor of terrorism. The provision at 252.225-7049 implements 10 U.S.C. 2279, which restricts acquisitions of commercial satellite services from any entity that is owned by the government of a covered foreign country (China, North Korea, or any state sponsor of terrorism) or that is planning or expected to provide or use launch or other satellite services under the contract from a covered foreign country.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Transitional Compensation (TC) for Abused Dependents
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This rule establishes policy, assigns responsibilities, and prescribes procedures governing the administration of transitional compensation (TC) for abused dependents. Transitional compensation is one of the many resources available to victims of domestic abuse. This program provides temporary monetary payments and military benefits to dependents of service members who have been separated from the military due to a domestic violence or child abuse offense. These benefits last from 12-36 months in accordance with the law. The intent of this benefit program is to encourage victims of domestic violence to come forward and report the abuse. It separates the victims from the abuser, informs the victims of the many resources available to them as a victim of domestic violence, ensures the safety and well-being of the victims, and ensures the Department of Defense does not leave a spouse and family financially destitute when the abusing spouse is discharged from the military for a dependent-abuse offense. In accordance with statute, the rate of payment varies based on the rank of the spouse, but is designed to cover living expenses such as food, clothing, and housing. The rule was last updated in 1995 and will be revised to reflect current practices and to remove internal content that is currently codified.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Unlawful Discrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance From, or Conducted by, the DoD
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is proposing to amend its regulations prohibiting unlawful discrimination on the basis of disability in programs or activities receiving Federal financial assistance from, or conducted by, DoD. These revisions update and clarify the obligations that section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended (section 504), imposes on recipients of Federal financial assistance and DoD Components, and the obligations that the Architectural Barriers Act imposes on DoD Components. The updates also clarify the procedures for resolving complaints regarding allegations that DoD Components failed to make information and communication technology accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities in accordance with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, as amended (section 508). Consistent with the DOJ section 504 coordination regulation, on April 8, 1982, DoD promulgated 32 CFR part 56, implementing section 504 within the Department. Thirty-four years later, there is a compelling need to clarify and update this regulation to ensure that DoD policies reflect the most current Federal law and policies regarding unlawful nondiscrimination on the basis of disability.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda
RIN_INFO.ADDITIONAL_INFO: DoD Instruction 1020.dd ("Unlawful Discrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance from, or Conducted by, the DoD") will be codified as a rule under 32 CFR part 56, as a rule revision. The rule was originally reported as being codified under 32 CFR part 195.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: DoD Privacy Program
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This proposed rule revises 32 CFR part 310 to implement section 552a of title 5, United States Code, the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, thus establishing procedures for access as well as other privacy protections. This part also promotes uniformity in the DoD Privacy Program, creating a single privacy rule for the Department, while incorporating other administrative changes. It simplifies locating the applicable DoD privacy rule, and its use of plain language ensures enhanced readability and understanding by the public. It takes precedence over all DoD component publications that supplement and implement the DoD Privacy program. It will supersede the current parts 310 through 329 and parts 505,701 and 806b to promote uniformity in the DoD Privacy program and streamline the existing rules.

This rule is a deregulatory action and will be the single, consolidated privacy rule for the Department at 32 CFR 310 that contains all the codified information required for the Department. Therefore, 32 CFR parts 311, 312, 313, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319, 320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 326, 327, 329, 505, 701, and 806b will be removed from the CFR after the rule at 32 CFR part 310 is finalized.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Stars and Stripes (S&S) Media Organization
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: Stars and Stripes (S&S) is authorized by Congress and the U.S. DoD to produce independent daily military news and information distributed at U.S. military installations in Europe and Mideast and East Asia. A weekly derivative product is distributed within the United States by its commercial publishing partners. Stars and Stripes is a non-appropriated fund organization, only partially subsidized by DoD. A large portion of its operating costs is earned through the sale of advertising and subscriptions. Unique among the many military publications, Stars and Stripes operates as a First Amendment newspaper and is part of the newly formed Defense Media Activity. This rule will update policies and authorities, and assign responsibilities and procedures which have not been updated since 1994. Internal content will be removed through this revision, but those parts of the rule require rulemaking will remain.  This includes (but is not limited to) advertising acceptance standards, the independence of the entity from that Government influence, and the rights of individuals who believe that S&S has infringed upon their civil liberties.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: DoD Newspapers, Magazines, Guides, and Installation Maps
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This rule establishes policy, assigns responsibilities, and prescribes procedures for establishing and managing the publication of authorized DoD newspapers, magazines, guides, and installation maps (referred to collectively in this rule as "DoD publications") to support the DoD Command Information Program. Commanders use DoD publications to communicate mission-essential information to members of the command, thereby facilitating accomplishment of the command's mission. News reports and stories printed in DoD publications about individuals and organizational elements of the command provide cross feed of information, improving internal cooperation and mission performance. In addition, recognition of excellence in individual and organizational performance motivates and sets expected norms for mission accomplishment.

RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This proposed rule will establish responsibilities and prescribe procedures for enforcing traffic laws on DoD installations in the United States.  Violations of State vehicular or pedestrian traffic laws on a DoD installation are subject to the fines and punishment under the criminal or civil law of the State, territory, possession, or district where the DoD installation in which the violation occurred is located.  This new rule will consolidate existing DoD rules and guidance to form a single DoD rule governing traffic laws.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Voluntary Education Programs
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This rule implements DoD’s Voluntary Education Programs to provide servicemembers with opportunities to enhance their academic achievement (i.e., earn a degree or certificate) during their off-duty time, which in turn improves job performance and promotion potential. This rule establishes the requirement for a standardized memorandum of understanding (MOU) between DoD and an educational institution before participating in DoD Voluntary Education Programs, including TA. While the rule is current as of May 15, 2014, the rule is being modified to increase its effectiveness and improve efficiencies. Streamlined processes and procedures, increased transparency, and requirements clarifications should reduce effort on the part of educational institutions (i.e., reduced manpower/resources to manage business processes or systems for compliance with rule). For example, the rule has five appendices, one for DoD and one for each of the Military Services (Air Force, Army, Marine Corps, and Navy). DoD is working with the Military Services to consolidate and streamline processes and procedures across DoD, thereby reducing the burden on educational institutions to comply with five differing requirements (i.e., identifying a school representative to liaison with each installation education official or reporting tuition rate changes to DoD and each of the Military Services).

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Discharge Review Board (DRB) Procedures and Standards
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
DoD is proposing revisions to create a single DoD-level rule for discharge and dismissals by incorporating language from all the Military Service rules which will be repealed once this revision is issued. This consolidated rule will include the latest information about Boards for Correction of Military/Naval Records (BCM/NRs) and Disability Review Boards (DRBs), current DoD policy on BCMRs and DRBs, Don't Ask Don't Tell policy, Post Traumatic Stress Disorder/Traumatic Brain Injury policy, all of which apply to both DRBs and BCM/NRs. This rule discusses the review of discharges or dismissals under 10 U.S.C. 1553; provides guidelines for discharge review by application or on motion of a Discharge Review Board (DRB), and the conduct of discharge reviews and standards to be applied in such reviews, which are designed to ensure historically consistent uniformity in execution of this function, as required under Pub. L. 95-126; assigns responsibility for administering the program; makes provisions for public inspection, copying, and distribution of DRB documents through the Armed Forces Discharge Review/Correction Board Reading Room; establishes procedures for the preparation of decisional documents and index entries; and provides guidance for processing complaints concerning decisional documents and index entries.

This part will be revised to create a single DoD-level rule by incorporating language from the Military Service rules, which will be repealed once this revision is issued. This part is being revised to include the latest information about Boards for Correction of Military/Naval Records (BCM/NRs) and Disability Review Boards, current DoD policy on BCMRs and DRBs, Don't Ask Don't Tell policy, and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder/Traumatic Brain Injury policy, all of which apply to both DRBs and BCM/NRs.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Financial Institutions on DoD Installations
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This part establishes policies and responsibilities for financial institutions that serve DoD personnel on DoD installations worldwide. In addition, the part prescribes consistent arrangements for the provision of services by financial institutions among the DoD components. Furthermore, the part requires that financial institutions operating on DoD installations provide, and are provided, support consistent with the policies stated. The Department’s policies have changed, and the current part requires revision to reflect the revised responsibilities and arrangements. The Department will retain 32 CFR part 230 as the single rule for DoD, pursuant to its revision. The Department will incorporate 32 CFR part 231 and thereafter repeal 32 CFR part 231. The maintaining and referencing of two parts in the CFR is unnecessary and redundant. Cost savings have not been identified.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Access to and Conduct on DoD Property

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Release of Official Information in Litigation and Testimony by DoD Personnel as Witnesses
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: The Touhy Regulation, as this rule is commonly known, prescribes procedures for the submission and processing of third-party litigation requests for information. It codifies DoD Directive 5405.2, issued to implement authorities afforded by the Housekeeping Statute, 5 U.S.C. 301, as interpreted by the Supreme Court in United States ex rel. Touhy v. Ragen, 340 U.S. 462 (1951). All Federal agencies have issued their own Touhy regulations, and private litigants refer to these regularly. DoD’s current Touhy Regulation has been in place since 1985 and will be updated.

RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This part establishes policy for the development and implementation, jointly with each State, of procedures for persons to apply to register to vote at recruitment offices of the Armed Forces, pursuant to section 1973gg of title 42, United States Code. This rule dictates that military recruitment offices shall distribute the National Voter Registration Form to each eligible citizen, and provide assistance in completing the form unless the applicant refuses such assistance.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Family Advocacy Program
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This final rule will establish policy and assign responsibilities for addressing child abuse and domestic abuse through the Family Advocacy Program (FAP). The FAP "Guidelines for Clinical Intervention for Persons Reported as Domestic Abusers" provides clinical guidelines for the FAP assessment, clinical rehabilitative treatment, and ongoing monitoring and risk management of individuals who have reported to FAP by means of an unrestricted report for domestic abuse against current or former spouses, or intimate partners. This rule broadens the scope of FAP services to include former and current same-sex spouses in a legal union recognized as a marriage by a State or other jurisdiction. This rule will extend benefits to same-sex spouses of military service members and DoD civilians following the June 26, 2013, U.S. Supreme Court decision to declare Section 3 of the Defense of Marriage Act unconstitutional.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Identification (ID) Cards for Members of the Uniformed Services, Their Dependents, and Other Eligible Individuals
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: DoD is finalizing policy for the issuing of distinct DoD ID cards. These cards shall be issued to uniformed servicemembers, their dependents, and other eligible individuals and will be used as proof of identity and DoD affiliation. This rule extends benefits to same-sex spouses of military servicemembers and DoD civilians, at the direction of the President and the Secretary of Defense, based on the June 26, 2013, U.S. Supreme Court decision to repeal section 3 of the Defense of Marriage Act. Additionally, the Department has identified family member and dependent benefits that may lawfully be provided to same-sex domestic partners of eligible DoD civilian employees and other eligible individuals and their children through modifications to DoD policies and regulations. These benefits are extended to same-sex domestic partners and, where applicable, children of same-sex domestic partners, once DoD civilian or other eligible individual and their same-sex domestic partner have signed the appropriate declaration attesting to the establishment of their same-sex domestic partnership.  This rule has been merged with, and will be finalized by, RIN 0790-AJ37.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: National Industrial Security Program: Procedures for Government Activities Relating to Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI)
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This part sets forth industrial security procedures and practices related to foreign ownership, control, or influence (FOCI) for U.S. Government activities to ensure maximum uniformity and effectiveness in DoD implementation of the National Industrial Security Program (NISP), in accordance with Executive Order 12829. DoD allows foreign investment consistent with the national security interests of the United States, as established by Executive Order 11858. DoD FOCI procedures are used to protect against foreign interests gaining unauthorized access to classified, export-controlled, or all communications security information (classified or unclassified), adversely affecting the performance of classified contracts, and undermining U.S. security and export controls.

The interim final rule currently in effect now duplicates a proposed amendment to 32 CFR Part 2004, NISP Directive” by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). The Director of NARA’s Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO) is responsible for implementing and monitoring Executive Branch implementation of the NISP, and the content of part 117 is more appropriately addressed in part 2004.  Once the amendment to part 2004 is complete, this final rule will remove part 117.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

TIMETABLE.TTBL_ACTION: Interim Final Rule Comment Period End

RIN_INFO.ADDITIONAL_INFO:

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Victim and Witness Assistance
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This new rule assists victims and witnesses of crimes committed in violation of the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ), and discusses the rights of crime victims under the UCMJ which are more extensive than those of witnesses. It also describes notification and assistance available to victims and witnesses of crime from initial contact through investigation, prosecution, confinement, and release. Finally, annual reporting requirements for assistance provided across the DoD to victims of and witnesses to crime, and legal assistance for crime victims is discussed.

The rights of victims are laid out in the rule.  The Military Services are required to provide legal counsel, known as Special Victims’ Counsel/Victims’ Legal Counsel, to assist victims of alleged sex-related offenses under Articles 120, 120(a), 120(b), 120(c), and 125 of the UCMJ. The Military Services are also required to establish a special victim capability comprised of specially trained criminal investigators, judge advocates, paralegals, and victim/witness assistance personnel to support victims of covered special victim offenses.

It discusses how DS Logon credential holders may maintain and update their DS Logon credential and manage their personal settings. Finally, it defines the permissions that DS Logon credential holders have to access their information, who has access to view and edit their information, and who is eligible to act on their behalf.

This rule finalizes updates to the CFR, addresses eligibility documentation requirements, and documentation requirements for the correction of Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) records, and updates the part to reflect NIST Federal Information Processing Standards. 

The burden imposed on members of the public is the information collection required by the part, the time required to complete the DD Form 1172-2. Greater accuracy in the average hourly wage of respondents resulted in a $4,836,000.00 decrease in the cost burden.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Revised Interim Implementation of Governmentwide Guidance for Grants and Cooperative Agreements
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This final rule is the first of a sequence of six documents that collectively establish for DoD grants and cooperative agreements an updated interim implementation of Governmentwide guidance on administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit requirements for Federal awards. This rule removes a part of the DoD Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARs) that DoD adopted on December 19, 2014, as its interim implementation of the guidance, pending completion of more extensive updates to the DoDGARs needed to implement the guidance on a longer-term basis. It replaces that part with a new DoDGARs part containing a revised interim implementation of the guidance.

 The revised implementation in the new part incorporates 10 other new DoDGARs parts. Those 10 other new parts, set out in rule documents following this one, do several things. First, they provide standard wording of general terms and conditions governing administrative requirements for DoD grant and cooperative agreement awards to educational, nonprofit, and governmental entities subject to the Governmentwide guidance. Second, they provide standard wording for general terms and conditions addressing national policy requirements for DoD grant and cooperative agreement awards to all types of entities. Third, they establish a standard format for DoD grant and cooperative agreement awards. Finally, they establish a central DoDGARs part with definitions of terms used in those regulations.

In conjunction with establishing the revised implementation of the Governmentwide guidance, this rule establishes seven subchapters within DoD’s chapter of the Grants and Agreements title of the Code of Federal Regulations. The purpose of the subchapters is to provide an organizing framework for the DoDGARs to make it easier for users of the regulations to locate the content that they need.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Administrative Requirements Terms and Conditions for Cost-Type Awards to Nonprofit and Governmental Entities
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This final rule is the third of a sequence of six rule documents that make updates to the DoD Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARs). This rule will add seven new DoDGAR parts to address the administrative requirements included in general terms and conditions of DoD cost-type grants and cooperative agreements awarded to institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, States, local governments, and Indian tribes. The administrative requirements are in areas such as financial and program management; property administration; recipient procurement procedures; financial, programmatic, and property reporting; and subawards. The new parts will establish a uniform way for approximately 100 DoD component awarding offices to organize the administrative requirements in their general terms and conditions. The new parts also provide standard wording of terms and conditions for the administrative requirements, with associated regulatory prescriptions for DoD components to provide latitude to vary from the standard wording where variation is appropriate.

RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This section of the CFR was last updated on 7 June 2013 (78 FR 34251) as part of the 
Post-9/11 GI Bill.  As both DoD and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) had responsibilities for implementation and wanted to ensure service members, veterans, and families were aware of the new program, the initial rule included significant information explaining the entire program and not just DoD responsibilities. When the part was last revised, it only included the responsibilities of DoD, and is now being repealed since it only applies to members of the Uniformed Services.  All responsibilities pertaining to persons who are not members of the Uniformed Services are addressed in current VA regulations and repeal of this rule will have no effect on VA regulations.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Background Checks on Individuals in DoD Child Care Services Programs
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This rule describes requirements for criminal history background checks, including reinvestigation and self-reporting, for individuals involved with delivering child care services. The rule is intended to support the workforce mission of the DoD and implement current law that covers individuals expected to have regular contact with children in the performance of child care services on a DoD installation or DoD-sanctioned program. This rule will be amended to remove references to the internal audience and include only information that affects civilians, military dependents, and DoD contractors.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

CONTACT.TITLE: Senior Program Analyst, Office of Family Readiness Policy, MC&FP

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Paternity Claims and Adoption Proceedings Involving Members and Former Members of the Armed Forces
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This final rule will remove DoD’s regulation concerning paternity claims and adoption proceedings involving members and former members of the Armed Forces. The DoD policy that corresponds with this rule was rescinded on 19 December 2011.  DoD empowers commanders to handle family and dependent care in accordance with local laws governing paternity and child support, and service standards for dependents.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Allotments for Child and Spousal Support
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This section of the CFR re-states DOD’s internal financial management regulation
statutorily required child or child and spousal support allotments forforfor members of the Military Services on extended active duty. Therefore, DoD is repealing this section of the CFR.  DoD internal guidance will continue to be published in DoD's Financial Management Regulation, Volume 7A, Chapter 41, Garnishments and Other Involuntary Allotments” available at http://comptroller.defense.gov/Portals/45/documents/fmr/archive/07aarch/07a_41_Dec10.pdf.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Defense Support of Special Events
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This final rule will remove DoD’s rule which establishes procedures and assigns responsibilities for Special Events because it is internal to the Department.  Although civil authorities and officials of qualifying entities may request support from DoD, this rule neither confers a benefit not otherwise provided for in statute nor imposes a burden on the public. Concurrently with the repeal of this part, DoD will provide notice in the Federal Register to inform the public how to submit requests for special event support.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda
RIN_INFO.ADDITIONAL_INFO: DoD internal guidance concerning defense support of special events will continue to be published in DoD Instruction 3025.20, Defense Support of Special Events" available at http://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/302520p.pdf.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Competitive Information Certificate and Profit Reduction Clause
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: 32 CFR 173.2, Competitive Information Certification, and 32 CFR 173.3, Profit Reduction Clause, were inserted into the Code of Federal Regulations in 1988, during an ongoing investigation of procurement practices known as Operation "Ill Wind." This part was intended for use until resolution of the investigation. The investigation was subsequently concluded and sanctions were imposed. Congress has subsequently enacted legislation to provide procurement integrity requirements, this part is no longer necessary.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Traffic and Vehicle Control on Certain Defense Mapping Agency Sites
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This final rule will remove the obsolete DoD part which applies to all areas in the Brookmont site and to all persons on or within the site. In this rule the Brookmont site refers to the grounds and facilities of the Defense Mapping Agency Hydrographic/Topographic Center (DMAHTC) and the Defense Mapping Agency Office of Distribution Services (DMAODS). The Defense Mapping Agency no longer exists; it became part of the National Imagery and Mapping Agency (NIMA) and the location of NIMA/NGA is no longer controlled by DoD.  This rule is obsolete, and the part will be removed.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Registration of Privately Owned Motor Vehicles
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT:
This final rule will remove the DoD rule which contains procedures for the registration,
inspection, and marking of privately owned vehicles (POV) on Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) activities. DoD Directive-Type Memorandum (DTM) 09-012, Interim Policy Guidance for DoD Physical Access Control, was published in September 2009 and defined new minimum standards for controlling access to DoD installations. Access control shifted from vehicle identification to personnel identification and validation of personnel identification credentials. DLA formally rescinded its policy, DLA Instruction 4309, Vehicle Registration,” on August 2, 2012. The rule is obsolete and will be repealed.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Transporter Proof of Delivery
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: The TPD clause provides a mechanism for procuring alternative proof of delivery from contractors. Documentation is used as evidence of receipt and acceptance of delivery facilitating timely payment and decreasing Prompt Payment Act interest charges against the Government.  DOD is continuing to discuss next steps on this rule and is withdrawing the RIN at this time.

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: DoD Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Program Regulation
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: The Department of Defense finalized a revision of its DoD-level FOIA regulation to incorporate the provisions of the OPEN Government Act of 2007 and the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016. This part promotes uniformity in the DoD FOIA Program across the entire Department. With the issuance of this final rule, 13 component FOIA regulations, as well as the second DoD-level regulation at 32 CFR part 285, will be repealed.

RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: This rule is being withdrawn for reconsideration by the Department pending revisions to part 103 of 32 CFR which will be done as a separate rulemaking.  This section of the CFR provides guidance and procedures for the SAPR Program. It includes establishing the processes and procedures for the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Kit; establishing the multidisciplinary Case Management Group (CMG), providing guidance on how to handle sexual assault; and establishing minimum program standards, training requirements, and requirements for the DoD Annual Report on Sexual Assault in the Military.
